messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: high 5xx/error-rate detected for inference gateway (/v1/generate). Priority: P1. Please ack.

alex.s: acked. looking now. seeing spike in 504/502 across gateway region-us-west2.

jamie.r: I'm seeing a matching spike on envoy upstream cluster 'model-pool-a'. 5xx rate ~18% over last 3m. Latency for successful requests also up.

priya.g: tagging in runtime team. Any recent deploys for routing/traffic policy?

deploy-bot: Deploy: routing-service v2026.03.14-2 went live 22m ago (canary -> 100%). No rollbacks.

mike.k: grafana: https://grafana.internal/alerts/12345 spike graph attached (paste). Looks like error spike started ~20m after deploy.

alex.s: grabbing envoy admin /clusters dump from a few front proxies. noting many upstream hosts in LB pool reporting 503.

jamie.r: suspecting retry policy + route weight change caused retry amplification to overloaded backend. The route in question has retries: 2 per attempt and max connection pool per-host is low.

priya.g: can we temporarily disable retries at the gateway to break the retry loop?

mike.k: yes. propose patching envoy route config to set "retry_policy" -> "num_retries": 0 for /v1/generate on region-us-west2.

alex.s: applying change to one edge cluster now (prod-edge-3). command: ```kubectl -n infra exec deploy/prod-edge-3 -- curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9901/config_dump -d@- <<'EOF'
# local edit: update route table
EOF
``` will route a short rolling restart after config update.

jamie.r: oncall, make sure we don't break downstream fallbacks. Set circuit-breaker thresholds a bit higher first? we can also increase max connections to reduce backpressure.

priya.g: quick customer-impact check: CS dashboard shows ~120 active requests failing in the last 5m, primarily from enterprise accounts on Dedicated. Notify acct owners?

lisa-cs: I'll draft an outbound note: "We're investigating elevated errors on text generation; mitigations in progress. No data loss suspected. ETA for resolution: 30-60 minutes."

deploy-bot: Patch applied to prod-edge-3: retries disabled for /v1/generate. Rolling to prod-edge-1,2 next.

alex.s: After disabling retries on edge-3, 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 7% on that edge within 45s. Latency improved slightly.

jamie.r: good sign. continue rolling to other edges but hold autoscale config - don't scale model pool yet, we might be hiding root cause.

mike.k: rolling to edge-1 and edge-2 now.

priya.g: while rolling, let's also inspect upstream model-pool-a: connection saturation logs show a flood of short-lived connections and many 503s from the model service indicating "backend overloaded / accept error".

alex.s: looks like the routing change from the recent deploy increased weight to model-pool-a by 3x for v2 model. That + retries caused retry storms.

jamie.r: root cause hypothesis: config rollout changed route weights without adjusting circuit-breaker and connection pool limits. Retries compounded failure, causing cascade.

priya.g: mitigation plan we executed: 1) disable gateway retries (done), 2) reduce route weight to model-pool-a by 50% (planned), 3) increase per-host connection limits on envoy, 4) apply temporary circuit-breaker to fail fast and direct to fallback model-pool-b.

mike.k: executing step 2 now: updating traffic weights via routing-service api: ```curl -X POST https://routing.internal/v1/weights -d '{"pool":"model-pool-a","weight":50}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'```

deploy-bot: traffic weight update accepted. New weight propagating across control-plane.

alex.s: after weight change, overall 5xx has fallen to ~3.5% cluster-wide. model-pool-a errors reduced too.

jamie.r: next, increase per-host connections on envoy to 200 from 80 on the affected clusters to ease head-of-line. We'll roll config canary first.

priya.g: also schedule a short canary rollback of routing-service deploy to previous version that had older weights, if we confirm config is the issue.

lisa-cs: CS update ready to send: "We've implemented mitigations (disabled automatic retries and adjusted routing) which has reduced errors considerably. We're monitoring and will follow up with a post-incident summary." Approving to send.

mike.k: canary rollback queued. If errors stay down for 10m, we'll keep current and do a postmortem.

alex.s: monitoring 10m window. Will collect traces for 502/503 to add to postmortem (x-request-id list).

jamie.r: post-incident action items (PIAs): 1) tighten deploy checks to detect large weight changes, 2) ensure retry policy defaults are safe (no amplification), 3) add gating alert for connection saturation on model pools, 4) run tabletop on retry amplification.

priya.g: adding PIA ticket now and assigning to eng-runtime and deployments.

incident-bot: Incident p1: "gateway retry amplification -> model-pool pressure" created: INC-2026-034. Linking to this thread.

alex.s: marking incident as mitigated for now (errors down to baseline ~0.8%). Keeping thread open for root-cause analysis.

lisa-cs: outbound sent to affected customers. Will follow up with postmortem draft. :thumbsup:

mike.k: thanks all. Great quick coordination. We'll publish timeline and RCA once we have traces/logs consolidated.

jamie.r: leaving oncall to alex.s in 15m for follow-up.

alex.s: ack handoff. I'll continue monitoring and compile logs.

priya.g: closing comments: remember to include the exact routing diff in the postmortem (who changed what).

alex.s: noted. end of thread for now.
